name: Orangish
lede: Orangish is a warm, salmon-leaning orange named simply for being nearly, but not quite, orange, carried in our data by both a general web source and the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A word that means almost orange
sections.body:
Orangish is built from [[orange]] plus the suffix *-ish*, softening grammar also used elsewhere in the library's descriptive names [1]. Our sources carry no author, pigment or standards body behind this exact value, only a general web listing and the 2010 xkcd survey; the origin stays undocumented in our data [1].

The nearest named look-alikes on file are [[coral|Coral]] and [[mandarin|Mandarin]], both almost the same shade [2]. That is itself a small lesson in crowd naming: a survey like xkcd's records whatever spelling and wording a visitor typed, with no settled standard behind it [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive, a close match turns up in 15 paintings, about 0.06 per cent, with the within-painting lens finding it in 16, rarer than 63 per cent of our named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1600s, at 1.4 times the archive's overall rate (6 paintings), and most often plays an accent [3]. The earliest match, by Sandro Botticelli and dated 1470, sits 540 years before the 2010 survey name; that gap is a floor, not a first sighting, as photographed, not a pigment match [3].
